Asking for a friend…

Dundertanding the domain of a competition is very often key. Is it true here?

Absolutely! Compared to other trading card games like MTG or Yu-Gi-Oh!, the rules of the Pokémon TCG are much simpler. It's designed so that even a 10-year-old can play it. Of course, just because the rules are simple doesn't necessarily mean it'll be an easy AI task to solve, though!
Don't underestimate 10 years old. They beat Adults at many things.

I'm in a worse position than your friend since I'm not really familiar with neither Pokemon nor RL literature 😅

As other mentioned, the rules are quite simple and the meta seems to be only a handful of decks so it's quite quick to get familiar with their mechanics. So, my gut feeling tells me that, although very useful, it's not necessary to get a good score as we can get a somewhat decent domain knowledge in a few days.
coding agents can mitigate the lack of RL knowledge. Not sure they can mitigate the lack of Pokemon experience. We'll see.
are you good at building harnnesses and good at math because i am feel that is the core of this competion
Play a few games yourself and you'll understand what's going on well enough to work on this

I made it to rank 50 just watching https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eKC5PlYoboE&t=1s and with basic RL principles I learnt from Orbit Wars. So totally possible. Going with a rule based approach probably needs quite a bit of domain knowledge though.

I am however struggling a bit to identify weaknesses at this point, so having domain knowledge or teaming up with someone who does seems important.
I got up to 12th at one point and I have never played anything besides the mobile TCG. I do collect tho :)
I also do not have any knowledgement about Pokemon, but I think it is possible as RL will educate itself by understanding itself
